options.content:
# AN EMPTY PANEL ON THIS BOARD IS AMBIGUOUS

**This board is live.** The client SDK emits over OTLP-HTTP to the GC telemetry proxy, the OTel collector accumulates and exports, and Prometheus scrapes it. Verified end to end from sdk-core's own built bundle through GC on the cluster - not a synthetic payload.

**That is exactly why empty no longer means one thing.** Before the exporter landed, an empty panel meant the pipeline was unwired and nothing else. Now it is ambiguous between *no drops occurred*, *no browser has been connected recently*, and *the pipeline broke*. **Do not read an empty panel as 'nothing bad happened' until you have discriminated.**

## The three-step discriminator

1. **`up{job="otel-collector"} == 1`** - is the collector being scraped at all? If not, every panel below is meaningless and the problem is the collector or the scrape, not the client.
2. **`count(dt_client_media_frames_received_total)`** - has *any* browser emitted within the collector's `metric_expiration` window? No result means no client has reported recently; it says nothing about drops. **This is the ONLY liveness signal for the client fleet** - there is no per-browser `up` and there structurally cannot be one, because a per-session `service.instance.id` is barred by ADR-0036 §11.
3. **Only if 1 and 2 both hold** does an empty drop panel mean zero drops.

(Step 2 depends on the collector's `metric_expiration`; the value lives in `infra/services/otel-collector/collector.yaml` and its derivation in `docs/observability/alert-conventions.md`. It is deliberately not restated here - a number copied onto a board outlives the config it was copied from.)

## This board's empty-panel meaning is the OPPOSITE of mh-media.json's

**Do not copy wording between the two boards.** On *Media Handler - Media Path*, an empty drop panel means no drops occurred - unambiguously the healthy state, because MH registers its media series eagerly at startup and they exist at zero whether or not anything flows. Here, client series are created lazily on first emission, so absence and zero are different states and only the discriminator above tells them apart. This distinction got *sharper* when the pipeline was fixed, not softer.

## Timestamps are collector-arrival, not browser-event

Delta points are restamped with the collector's clock. Values are correct, but a spike here may be an artefact rather than a burst: session teardown force-flushes pending deltas at one instant, a backgrounded tab flushes on resume, and a collector outage **re-dates** whatever the browsers buffered across it. Full reading guidance: `docs/observability/metrics/client.md` §Stored series shape.

## Key custody

`key_custody=operator`. The client encrypts media; MC holds the per-meeting KEK and can read it; MH, transport and storage cannot. That is accepted operator custody, **not end-to-end and not zero-trust** (ADR-0036 §4).

Triage for the key-material path: `docs/runbooks/mc-incident-response.md` Scenario 16: Missing Key Material.

panels.title: READ FIRST - how to read an empty panel on this board

panels.description: The two ends of the receive-path accounting identity received = accepted + sum(drops by reason), ratified in docs/observability/metrics/client.md. received is counted AT THE WIRE before any parse or verification; accepted is counted after the frame opened. A gap between them that the drop panel does not explain means the identity is broken and one of the three counters has a missing emission site. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Receive Path - Frames Received / Accepted

panels.description: Frames the receive path could not open, by frozen reject reason. THE SIGNAL THIS BOARD EXISTS FOR: the three key-material reasons no_kek_for_generation (KEK generation newer than held - MC's push has not arrived), kek_generation_stale (generation older than this client retains) and no_roster_entry are, per ADR-0036 §11, the only signal for a join or rotation path that has silently stopped delivering keys - all are expected transiently at join and after a KEK rotation, and sustained is the fault. Split on reason FIRST; the three arms have different remedies and are not equally instrumented. EMPTY HERE IS NOT A STATEMENT ABOUT DROPS AT ALL. Today it means the export hop is unwired (see the banner), and it would look exactly the same whether or not frames were being dropped. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE MH MEDIA-PATH BOARD, where the drop panels read a flat ZERO when healthy (those counters are present-at-zero from startup; an ABSENT series there is a fault). Do not carry that reading across to this board; once the exporter lands, an empty panel here will mean what it means there, and not before. The discriminator, once both states are possible: count(dt_client_media_frames_received_total) returning no data (series absent, pipeline unwired) versus returning a number (series present, counters genuinely at zero). No client reject reason is video-gated - every token that can appear on this counter is reachable in this story. Stated explicitly because the equivalent MH drop panels DO name two reasons that cannot fire until video, and silence here would be indistinguishable from having forgotten to check. There is deliberately no 'or vector(0)' in this query: it would fabricate a series and flatten the by-reason breakdown that triage depends on.
panels.title: Receive Path - Frame Drops by Reason

panels.description: Wrapped-key outcomes on frames that were ACCEPTED - neither value ever reaches the drop counter, and counting one as a drop would silently break the receive-path accounting identity. kek_generation_not_held means one key id arrived under a second wrap and the frame played off a cached transmit key. An honest sender of this SDK cannot produce it: on every KEK change it rotates to a NEW key id (R-13), which arrives uncached and lands on the DROP reasons instead. A sustained non-zero rate therefore means a non-conforming or hostile sender that re-wraps rather than rotates, NOT rotation lag. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Receive Path - Non-Dropping Wrapped-Key Outcomes

panels.description: Gap frames and reorder events on the downlink, plus terminal decoder errors. Gaps and reorders are network-shaped; decoder errors are terminal AudioDecoder failures and carry no reason label by design (AudioDecoder provides no bounded vocabulary, and an unbounded one here is the cardinality hazard ADR-0036 §11 exists to prevent). AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Receive Path - Downlink Continuity and Decode

panels.description: Frames arriving on a relay stream_id this client never declared in its ReceiveCapability. The relay region is UNAUTHENTICATED - a handler writes stream_id freely and nobody signs it - so an undeclared value creates no receiver state and is counted here instead; the frame is still verified and attributed from its own key id. A sustained rate means a handler is routing to slots this subscriber did not ask for. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Receive Path - Undeclared Stream IDs

panels.description: Datagrams that left the device on the media datagram path; the denominator for the send-drop ratio. ONE INCREMENT PER TARGET HANDLER PER CAPTURED FRAME, NOT ONE PER FRAME: a sender whose edges span two handlers (ADR-0036 §9) advances this TWICE for one captured frame, so this is not a capture rate and must not be read as one. THE NAME SAYS FRAMES AND THE VALUE COUNTS DATAGRAMS - deliberately, matching dt_client_media_frames_received_total, which has counted datagrams-at-the-wire since story 1. Both ends of the ratio are therefore in the same unit: the send-drop counter is raised inside the per-lane send path, so counting frames here would make one captured frame that succeeded on handler A and was refused on handler B read as 50% loss on a sender that reached A perfectly. MUTE IS NOT VISIBLE HERE AND MUST NOT BE INFERRED FROM IT: while client-muted nothing is encoded, so nothing is sent and nothing is dropped. Muted, silent and the-network-died are indistinguishable from absence alone - read the mute-transitions panel. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Send Path - Datagrams Sent

panels.description: Frames the send path discarded, by a bounded send-drop vocabulary that is DISTINCT from the receive reject taxonomy. Every spelling EXCEPT `not_connected` deliberately matches MH's MediaDropReason, so `sum by(reason)` compares across the two ends of one hop; `not_connected` is client-only, because MH never initiates. The roster's one home is `MEDIA_SEND_DROP_REASONS` in `packages/sdk-core/src/media/setup/mediaMetrics.ts`, which a `toEqual` test pins - the correspondence is stated here by naming the exception, never by a count, so it cannot go stale on a sixth token. transport_send_refused and not_connected should both READ ZERO FOREVER. EMPTY HERE IS NOT A STATEMENT ABOUT DROPS AT ALL. Today it means the export hop is unwired (see the banner), and it would look exactly the same whether or not frames were being dropped. THIS IS THE OPPOSITE OF THE MH MEDIA-PATH BOARD, where the drop panels read a flat ZERO when healthy (those counters are present-at-zero from startup; an ABSENT series there is a fault). Do not carry that reading across to this board; once the exporter lands, an empty panel here will mean what it means there, and not before. The discriminator, once both states are possible: count(dt_client_media_frames_received_total) returning no data (series absent, pipeline unwired) versus returning a number (series present, counters genuinely at zero). No client reject reason is video-gated - every token that can appear on this counter is reachable in this story. Stated explicitly because the equivalent MH drop panels DO name two reasons that cannot fire until video, and silence here would be indistinguishable from having forgotten to check. There is deliberately no 'or vector(0)' in this query: it would fabricate a series and flatten the by-reason breakdown that triage depends on.
panels.title: Send Path - Send Drops by Reason

panels.description: Depth of the DEEPEST of the sender's bounded egress lanes (one per target handler, each bounded independently), in frames. A full gauge with healthy frames_sent means ONE lane (one handler's path) is stalled, not the sender. Read against the configured bound - `media.egress.maxQueueFrames` and `media.audio.frameDurationMs` in `packages/sdk-core/src/config/clientConfig.ts` (10 frames x 20 ms = 200 ms at the defaults in force at time of writing; cited rather than restated so the figure cannot silently drift from the config). The application bound trips BEFORE the transport high-water mark - asserted at setup - so a rising depth here is back-pressure we can count rather than loss inside the user agent. NOT an egress budget, capacity or ceiling: no such gauge exists in this story. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Send Path - Egress Queue Depth

panels.description: KEK arrivals through the KEK-source seam by source, and client mute transitions by action. Neither carries key material or a KEK generation - the generation is monotonic over a meeting's life, so as a label its cardinality is unbounded over TIME and a per-meeting generation series would be a membership-change trace. Client mute is enforced at CAPTURE and does not depend on the server honouring it. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Key and Mute Lifecycle

panels.description: Wall-clock milliseconds from media pipeline start to the first media frame arriving at the wire. Despite the name's resemblance to dt_client_time_to_first_mh_connected_ms this is NOT a frozen-roster member and carries the media-path label set, not the join-flow one - it has no meeting dimension of any kind. No objective attaches to it in this story. AN EMPTY PANEL HERE IS AMBIGUOUS - it does not by itself mean zero drops. Run the three-step discriminator in the READ FIRST panel before concluding anything from absence.
panels.title: Time to First Media Frame (p95 / p50)

panels.description: dt_client_media_capture_source{mode}: what feeds each client's send path, as a presence gauge (value 1 for the ACTIVE mode only; a microphone build never writes a test_tone series). A test_tone series in any environment other than dev/test means a test-tone build (the Vite build-time define __DT_TEST_TONE__, story 2 R-7) is serving real users whose microphones are not being sent at all. Presence is judged over the lookback window, not per scrape: the SDK re-sets the gauge once per export interval on its own timer. No alert, deliberately - dev and test legitimately carry test_tone and the environment is not on the series. See docs/observability/metrics/client.md.
panels.title: Send Path - Capture Source (SAFETY: test_tone outside dev)

panels.description: dt_client_media_receive_source_deficit_total, unit assignment-intervals: per export interval, the number of ACTIVE receive assignments (MC assigned a sender and did not mark it source-muted) from which the client decoded NO frame for the whole interval. Observed decode activity is the receiver's ground truth; a rising line means MC claims a live source and nothing decodes. Plotted as increase(): silent assignment-intervals per step. rate(...) multiplied by the SDK's metric export interval (config key telemetry.metricExportIntervalMs, deliberately not restated here) is the mean number of silent active assignments fleet-wide. Premise: DTX is off, so a live sender always produces frames. BLIND to a declaration MC rejected whole (no active assignments) - see the Receive-Slot Refusals panel. Triage: docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md.
panels.title: Receive Path - Silent Active Sources (deficit)

panels.description: dt_client_media_receive_slots_rejected_total: startMedia() calls the SDK refused because the client's declared receive-slot count N (VITE_DT_RECEIVE_SLOTS) exceeds the cap MC advertised on JoinResponse.max_receive_slots (MC_MAX_RECEIVE_SLOTS). MC would reject the whole declaration, so the client refuses loudly and receives nothing. Reads zero on a correctly configured deployment. The deficit panel stays at 0 for this failure - this panel is its only signal. With an MC that predates the field, the same failure counts on MC's mc_media_receive_capability_declarations_total{outcome="slot_count_over_cap"} instead. Triage: docs/runbooks/client-dev-local.md.
panels.title: Receive Path - Receive-Slot Refusals (N over MC cap)
